subject: math

objective.text: Draw equal groups with circles. Write a repeated addition equation to find the total.

source_ref.section: Lesson objective

explanations.title: Add the groups
explanations.text: 4 groups have 3 counters each. To find the total, add the number in each group. 3 plus 3 plus 3 plus 3 equals 12. This is repeated addition.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (4 groups of 3)

explanations.title: Draw groups of circles
explanations.text: In math, we draw circles to show groups. Draw a big circle for each group. Draw the same number of small circles in each. Draw a line under each group.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (draw circles)

explanations.title: The repeating number
explanations.text: The number that repeats is how many are in each group. The number of times it repeats is how many groups there are. 4 groups of 3 gives 3 plus 3 plus 3 plus 3.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (S: The 3 stands for how many are in each group)

explanations.title: Say it in words
explanations.text: You can say 3 plus 3 plus 3 plus 3 equals 12 as 4 groups of 3 equals 12. For 3 groups of 5, you can also say 3 fives equals 15.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (3 fives equals 15)

examples.title: 4 groups of 3
examples.text: 4 groups of 3 counters. Write 3 under each group. 3 plus 3 equals 6. 6 plus 3 equals 9. 9 plus 3 equals 12. 4 groups of 3 equals 12.

misconceptions.label: Adds the number of groups instead of the number in each group
misconceptions.description: The child adds the number of groups. For 4 groups of 3, the child writes 4 plus 4 plus 4 plus 4. The repeated number must be how many are in each group.
detection_signals: Says or writes the number of groups as the repeated addend, for example 4 plus 4 plus 4 plus 4 for 4 groups of 3.
Cannot say what the repeated number shows.
misconceptions.response_text: Look at one group. It has 3 circles. So we add 3 each time. We add 3 four times because there are 4 groups.

assets_required.why_this_method: Exact group counts, small circles in each group, number lines under each group and a growing equation need exact behaviour. Diffusion cannot count.
assets_required.description: Groups drawn as big circles. Small circles (or stars) sit inside each group. A line sits under each group. The addition shows as the groups are added.
must_show_exactly: Exactly stimulus.per_group small shapes inside every group
Same shape in every group (circle by default, star when stimulus.shape is star)
states_or_frames: numbers appear under each group one at a time
running total shown step by step (for example 3, 6, 9, 12)
assets_required.interaction: Tutor sets groups and per_group from the stimulus. Numbers under the groups can be shown or hidden. Child answers by voice or typing.
assets_required.alt_text: Groups of small circles with a line under each group.
assets_required.generation_caption: Simple flat groups: big outlined circles with the same number of small dots in each, a short line under each, plain background. [Build by code]

assets_required.why_this_method: Diffusion may draw ONE sock icon in a child-friendly style. Code must lay out exactly 4 socks in each of 4 colours.
assets_required.description: 16 socks sorted into 4 colour groups of 4: purple, yellow, pink and orange.
must_show_exactly: Each colour is its own group
states_or_frames: 4 groups of 4 socks sorted by colour
assets_required.interaction: Display only. Child answers by voice or typing.
assets_required.alt_text: Sixteen socks sorted into four groups of four colours.
assets_required.generation_caption: ICON ONLY: one cartoon sock, flat colourful style, white background. (Code makes 4 copies in each of 4 colours.)
